+## #688 - Documentation site on GitHub Pages, built with Zola (first cut)
+
+**Decided:** a Zola project at `site/` with original Tera templates and one
+hand-written stylesheet (no third-party theme, no CSS framework, no
+JavaScript), a user guide (install, first run, setups, operations,
+posting, reading a refusal) and a short developer section (crate map,
+commands and undo, test gates, releases). It is built and deployed by two
+new jobs in the existing tag-triggered `release.yml`: `site` (install a
+pinned Zola, build) and `pages` (deploy with `actions/deploy-pages`). No
+trigger was added. The `/app/` browser build waits for #31; the front page
+says it is coming.
+
+**Why, choice by choice:**
+- **No theme.** A theme would add a licence to track in
+  `assets/ui/LICENSES.md` and styling we would have to read for
+  clean-room fit; four small templates and ~60 lines of CSS do the job and
+  stay readable. Light and dark follow `prefers-color-scheme`.
+- **Zola pinned to v0.23.6**, the musl Linux binary from the official
+  release, checked against its SHA-256 (the release asset's published
+  digest) - the same pattern the Linux job uses for linuxdeploy. musl,
+  because it is static and does not depend on the runner's glibc.
+- **Version from the workspace manifest, not from Zola.** Zola's
+  `load_data` refuses paths outside the site directory, so the templates
+  cannot read `../Cargo.toml`. The `site` job reads
+  `[workspace.package] version`, refuses a tag that does not name it
+  (as `publish` does), and writes `site/version.toml`, which the templates
+  load with `required=false`. A local build without the file says it is a
+  local preview instead of showing a version it was not built from. A
+  committed symlink into the site was dropped: Windows checkouts without
+  symlink support would get a text file and a broken build.
+- **Base URL from the repository**, `https://<owner>.github.io/<repo>`,
+  passed as `zola build --base-url`, so the same job deploys correctly on
+  NeoTech/Camcraft and on a fork's own Pages. `actions/configure-pages`
+  was dropped: it needs Pages API access in the build job and fails when
+  Pages is not yet enabled.
+- **Deploy after `publish`.** `pages` needs `site` and `publish` and runs
+  only on a tag when both succeeded, so the site's "Download X.Y.Z" link
+  never points at a release page that is not up. A run whose publish
+  fails leaves the previous site live. The `site` job also runs on a
+  manual `workflow_dispatch` as a build check; nothing is deployed then.
+- **Permissions scoped to the deploy job.** The workflow default stays
+  `contents: read`; only `pages` gets `pages: write` and `id-token: write`,
+  with a `pages` concurrency group so two tag runs never deploy at once.
+- **Nothing generated is committed:** `site/public/` and
+  `site/version.toml` are gitignored.
+
+**Content sources:** README, AGENTS.md, RELEASE_NOTES.md,
+`docs/MACHINE-ONBOARDING.md`, and the UI and app code for button labels,
+tab names, operation captions (`operation::KindInfo::ALL`) and refusal
+messages (`posting.rs`, `ui/egui_app/post_refusal.rs`). Only CamCraft's own
+behaviour is described; no vendor text was read or copied.
+
+**Not done here (follow-ups on #688):**
+- AGENTS.md's release steps do not name the site step yet. That is a
+  process-file change (a `PROCESS_VERSION` bump and a #681 note), so it is
+  left for the maintainer or a process PR once this job has run once.
+- Repository settings the deploy needs, which a workflow cannot set:
+  Pages source "GitHub Actions", and the `github-pages` environment's
+  deployment rules must allow tags matching `v*.*.0` (the default allows
+  only protected branches, which would refuse a tag deploy).
+- The Actions minutes of the first tag run are measured and reported on
+  #688 after that run.
+
+**Cost to change later:** low. Content is plain Markdown; switching the
+generator or adding the `/app/` folder (#31) touches only `site/` and the
+`site` job.

+# CamCraft documentation site
+
+The source of the CamCraft documentation site (#688), built with
+[Zola](https://www.getzola.org/) (a single binary; no Node toolchain).
+
+```sh
+cd site
+zola serve          # preview at http://127.0.0.1:1111

+The version shown on the site comes from `version.toml`, which the release

+The site is built and deployed by the `site` and `pages` jobs of
+`.github/workflows/release.yml`, on a release tag only. Write content from
+CamCraft's own code and docs: the clean-room protocol in `AGENTS.md`
+applies here too.

++++
+title = "CamCraft"
+sort_by = "weight"
+template = "index.html"
++++
+
+CamCraft is a CAM program: you import a 3D model, describe the stock, the
+work offset and the tools, add machining operations, and post an NC program
+(G-code) for your mill or lathe. It runs on Windows, Linux, macOS and
+FreeBSD, and it is written in Rust.
+
+Every toolpath is checked against the part, the stock, the fixtures and the
+machine before it can be posted. When CamCraft cannot show that a program is
+safe, it refuses to write it and says why.
+
+> **Pre-1.0 software.** CamCraft changes quickly. Treat every posted program
+> as a first draft: check it in your machine's own simulation and dry-run it
+> with the spindle off and Z raised before cutting material.
+
+**CamCraft in the browser is coming.** A WebAssembly build that runs in a
+current browser, with nothing to install, will be published on this site
+once the app and its interface build for the web
+([#31](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/31)). Until then, use the
+desktop downloads.

++++
+title = "Commands and undo"
+description = "Every change to the document is an undoable command."
+weight = 2
++++
+
+## Everything is a command
+
+A change to the document is never a direct field write from the UI. It is
+a **command**: a value that knows how to apply itself to the ECS world and
+how to invert itself exactly.
+
+```rust
+pub trait Command {
+    /// Forward effect.
+    fn apply(&self, world: &World);
+    /// Exact inverse of `apply`.
+    fn invert(&self, world: &World);
+}
+```
+
+The history (`History` in `crates/app/src/commands/mod.rs`) is a linear
+undo/redo stack of executed commands, and it is the single source of
+truth for what undo (Ctrl+Z) and redo (Ctrl+Y) can do. Executing a new
+command clears the redo stack. The history also tracks the depth at the
+last save, so undoing back to the saved point makes the document clean
+again.
+
+Examples: `CreateOperation`, `DeleteOperation`, `ChangeTool`,
+`EditOperationParams`, `SetStock`, `SelectEntity`, `ActivateSetup`,
+`LoadMachine`, `SetUnits`. Ephemeral view state (hover, camera, drag
+previews, the simulation's playback position) is immediate-mode and not
+undoable.
+
+## Validate at construction
+
+A command checks its input when it is built, not when it runs. A malformed
+stock, an empty setup name or a no-op change is refused with a
+`CommandError` that names the problem, so bad input never enters the
+history, and `apply` / `invert` are plain writes that cannot fail halfway.
+
+## Commands ship with an MCP tool
+
+`camcraft-cli mcp` runs a Model Context Protocol server that lets an AI
+agent drive CamCraft headlessly: import models, set stock, add tools and
+operations, generate, verify and post. Its tools (in
+`crates/app/src/mcp/`) call the same undoable commands the GUI uses, so
+the history and every check hold the same way. A pull request that adds a
+user-facing command also adds its MCP tool, or files a follow-up issue for
+it.
+
+## Deleting frees everything
+
+Deleting an entity frees every resource attached to it, for example the
+cached toolpath and rest-material meshes of a deleted operation. A leak is
+treated as a critical bug.

++++
+title = "Crate map"
+description = "The workspace crates and how they depend on each other."
+weight = 1
++++
+
+CamCraft is a Cargo workspace. Each crate holds one concern.
+
+| Crate | Package | Role |
+|---|---|---|
+| `crates/geometry` | `camcraft-geometry` | Meshes, slicing, 2D regions, mesh repair |
+| `crates/cl` | `camcraft-cl` | The cutter-location (CL) move stream |
+| `crates/tools` | `camcraft-tools` | Tool library and tool laws |
+| `crates/motion` | `camcraft-motion` | Toolpath generators: 2D, 3D, drilling, multi-axis, turning |
+| `crates/sim` | `camcraft-sim` | Stock simulation and the verifier |
+| `crates/post` | `camcraft-post` | The `.cps` post-processor engine and the standalone `post` binary |
+| `crates/kernel` | `camcraft-kernel` | The B-rep kernel seam: a thin `Kernel` trait (primitives, booleans, offset, blends, measure) and the bench that compares candidate engines |
+| `crates/app` | `camcraft-app` | Document model on a Flecs ECS world, commands with undo/redo, operations, posting, the `camcraft-cli` binary and its MCP server |
+| `crates/ui` | `camcraft-ui` | The egui desktop interface |
+| `xtask` | `xtask` | Project tooling: the test gates, packaging and release steps |
+
+`assets/` holds the post processors (`assets/posts/*.cps`), machine
+definitions (`assets/machines/*.mch`), UI icons, fonts and themes.
+`testdata/` holds the test models.
+
+## Layering
+
+The layering is strict: **ui → app → flecs**. UI panels, widgets and
+dialogs never touch the ECS world directly; they queue commands, and only
+app-layer commands and systems make raw Flecs calls. ECS components are
+declared in one place, `crates/app/src/schema.rs`, and are registered for
+every binary at startup.
+
+## Code shape
+
+- Source files stay under about 400 lines; a growing file is split along
+  its domain seam. Post-processor scripts are exempt: a `.cps` file is one
+  script the post engine runs whole.
+- Every module starts with a one-line provenance comment: what it
+  implements and which public source it was written from.
+- No platform-specific assumptions in core code: the same source builds on
+  Windows, Linux, macOS and FreeBSD.
+
+## Never crash, never gouge
+
+The project's first rule: output is correct, or it is refused with a
+diagnostic. `unwrap()`, `expect()` and `panic!()` are not used outside
+tests; errors are handled or propagated. Degenerate input (zero-area
+triangles, broken STEP files, nonsense tolerances) gives a clean error, not
+a crash or a hang. Anything a collision check or simulation flags as unsafe
+blocks the post.
+
+## Clean room
+
+CamCraft reimplements user-visible behaviour (operation types, parameters,
+workflow) from public documentation, G-code standards (RS-274, ISO 6983)
+and machining handbooks. No vendor code, text, icons, tool libraries or
+post processors are read or copied, and new toolpath algorithms are written
+from published technical literature. The full protocol is in `AGENTS.md`.

++++
+title = "Test gates"
+description = "Three gate tiers, run locally with cargo xtask gate."
+weight = 3
++++
+
+Tests run locally, on any OS, through one command from the workspace's
+`xtask/` crate: `cargo xtask gate <tier>`. There are three tiers, so a
+change is never held up by hours of unrelated tests.
+
+| Tier | When | What it runs | Target |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| `quick` | every change | only the test binaries and test functions the diff touches, in debug | 5 minutes or less |
+| `batch` | before a batch of commits | every debug suite except the slow ones, the UI suites, and clippy | 20 minutes or less |
+| `release` | at a release cut | everything, including the ignored heavy lanes in release mode | as long as it takes |
+
+```sh
+cargo xtask gate quick                 # what this branch touches, against main
+cargo xtask gate quick --base main     # name the base explicitly
+cargo xtask gate batch
+cargo xtask gate release
+cargo xtask gate test <name> [--crate c] [--exact]   # one test
+cargo xtask gate quick --dry-run       # print the plan, run nothing
+```
+
+Logs go to `gate-logs/<tier>-<timestamp>/`. The scripts
+`scripts/gate.ps1` and `scripts/gate.sh` are thin wrappers that forward to
+`cargo xtask gate`.
+
+## Test the change, not everything
+
+A fix is proved by the tests that pin it, run one by one. A whole suite
+runs only when the change touches what that suite covers; each suite's
+header names the modules it covers (its gate map), and `quick` picks
+suites from those maps.
+
+## Where tests live
+
+- `crates/app/tests/`: app and command tests, with shared fixtures in
+  `tests/common/`.
+- `crates/ui/tests/`: UI tests that start the real app; run them with the
+  working directory `crates/ui`.
+- Each other crate carries its own tests. Golden toolpath and G-code
+  outputs live under `tests/golden/`.
+- Tests that take more than about a minute in debug are marked
+  `#[ignore]` with their heavy lane named, and run in the release tier.
+- UI pixel snapshots run only in the release tier. A pull request never
+  changes a snapshot PNG; structural tests assert what each snapshot
+  guards, as text that holds on every OS.
+
+## GitHub Actions
+
+Nothing runs on push or pull request: Actions minutes are budgeted. GitHub
+runs only `release.yml`, on a pushed release tag, to build and publish the
+release (and this site). The CI and nightly workflows can be started by
+hand.

++++
+title = "Releases"
+description = "Versions, issues, pull requests and the release cut."
+weight = 4
++++
+
+## Versions
+
+Versions follow semantic versioning, derived from the commits since the
+last tag (Conventional Commits: `feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:` and so on):
+
+| Commits since the last tag | Release |
+|---|---|
+| a breaking change (`feat!:`, `fix!:` or a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer) | major (minor while the major is 0) |
+| any `feat` | minor |
+| only `fix`, `perf` or `refactor` | no release of its own; ships in the next minor |
+| only `docs`, `test`, `ci`, `build` or `chore` | no release |
+
+Only minor and major releases are cut, as `vX.Y.0` tags.
+
+## From issue to main
+
+Work is tracked as GitHub issues, picked by priority (`P0` wrong output,
+gouge, crash or data loss; `P1` wrong behaviour a user hits; `P2` owed
+polish) and weighted by effort (`effort:low` to `effort:max`).
+
+1. **Claim** the issue with a comment before writing code.
+2. **Branch** from the latest `main` (`issue/<N>-<short-name>`).
+3. **Fix** it with a test that pins the change, and record any decision
+   taken in `docs/decisions/<N>-<slug>.md`.
+4. **Gate** it with `cargo xtask gate quick`.
+5. **Open a draft pull request** that says what changed, how it was
+   tested, what was not exercised, a `Changelog:` line, and ends
+   `Fixes #N` (or `Refs #N` for partial work).
+6. The PR is flagged ready once its gates hold, then **reviewed** by a
+   reviewer that did not write it. `main` is protected: every change
+   reaches it through a pull request, with merge commits only.
+
+A `fix`, `perf` or `refactor` PR merges once its review is clean. A `feat`
+or breaking PR merges at the next release cut.
+
+## The release cut
+
+1. **Review and merge** the waiting feature PRs into `main`.
+2. **Release branch** `release/vX.Y.Z` from `main`:
+   `cargo xtask decisions --version X.Y.Z` gathers the decision files into
+   `RECOMMENDED.md`; the release notes and `CHANGELOG.md` rows are written;
+   then `cargo xtask release --version X.Y.Z --no-tag` runs the release
+   gate tier, bumps the version and builds the packages.
+3. **Release PR** `chore(release): X.Y.Z`, reviewed and merged like any
+   other.
+4. **Tag** the release merge commit `vX.Y.Z` and push the tag. The tag
+   starts `release.yml`, which builds every platform, publishes the GitHub
+   release with its assets, and builds and publishes this site from the
+   same tagged tree.
+
+Each release overwrites the site, so it always documents the latest
+release; older versions stay on the
+[releases page](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/releases).

@@ -0,0 +1,63 @@
++++
+title = "First run"
+description = "The window, the ribbon, and a first toolpath."
+weight = 2
++++
+
+## The window
+
+- **The ribbon** across the top holds the commands, in groups:
+  - **File:** New (Ctrl+N), Model (open a mesh model, Ctrl+O), Open (a
+    project, Ctrl+Shift+O), Save (Ctrl+S), Save As (Ctrl+Shift+S) and Post
+    (Ctrl+P).
+  - **Setup:** Setups, Stock, Origin (the work offset), Tools and the
+    machine button, which switches the workspace between Milling, Turning
+    and Mill-turning.
+  - **Operation groups** for the machine you are on: Milling 2D, Milling
+    3D, Drilling and Multi-axis on a mill; Turning on a lathe. Each group
+    opens a list of its operations. Right-click an operation to pin it to
+    the ribbon (up to four pins).
+  - **Modify:** Undo (Ctrl+Z), Redo (Ctrl+Y), Run (generate the selected
+    operation) and Delete.
+  - **Inspect:** Frame (F), Paths (show every toolpath), Simulate and
+    Deviate.
+  - **View:** Panels (show or hide the browser, properties and machines
+    panes, or reset the layout) and Theme.
+- **The browser** lists the document: models, setups with their stock,
+  machine, post, fixtures and tools, and the operations.
+- **The properties pane** shows the page of whatever you selected.
+- **The viewport** shows the model, stock, toolpaths and simulation.
+
+Hover any ribbon button to read what it does. A greyed-out operation says
+why in its tooltip, for example "No tool yet - add one (Setup > Tools)" or
+"No stock yet - set up stock first (Setup > Stock)".
+
+## A first toolpath
+
+1. **Import a model.** Click **Model** and pick an STL, OBJ or STEP file. If
+   an imported mesh has holes, the model's page has **Repair mesh**, which
+   welds vertices and fills holes and reports what it changed.
+2. **Set the stock.** Click **Stock**. The stock is a box, a cylinder, or a
+   copy of a model.
+3. **Place the work offset.** Click **Origin** to set the work coordinate
+   system (WCS) the program is written in.
+4. **Add a tool.** Click **Tools**, then **New tool…**. Fill in the
+   cutter's type and size. Tool libraries can be exported and imported as
+   `.camtools` files.
+5. **Add an operation.** Pick one from an operation group, for example
+   **Face** under Milling 2D. Its page opens with tabs: Geometry, Heights,
+   Passes, Lead in / Lead out, Feeds (and Machine for a few kinds). A kind
+   only shows the tabs it has settings for.
+6. **Generate.** Click **Generate** at the bottom of the page. **Apply**
+   commits edited settings without generating; **Clear toolpath** removes
+   the path but keeps the operation.
+7. **Check it.** Use **Simulate** to play the program against the stock,
+   and **Deviate** to compare the machined stock with the model.
+8. **Save** the project (`.camproj`) and [post](@/guide/posting.md) it.
+
+## Undo
+
+Every change to the document is a command, so Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y step
+through all of it: imports, stock, tools, operation settings, setups and
+theme changes. Moving the view, hovering and the simulation's playback
+position are not part of the history.

++++
+title = "Install"
+description = "Download a release for your system, or build from source."
+weight = 1
++++
+
+Releases are published on the
+[GitHub releases page](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/releases). Each
+release carries builds for Windows x64, Linux x86_64, macOS (universal, Apple
+Silicon and Intel), FreeBSD amd64 and Arch Linux.
+
+## Windows
+
+- **Portable zip:** unzip it anywhere and run `camcraft-ui.exe`.
+- **Installer** (`camcraft-<version>-win-x64-setup.exe`): installs for the
+  current user, without an administrator prompt.
+
+## Linux
+
+- **DEB or RPM:** install the package and start **CamCraft** from the
+  application menu, or run `camcraft`.
+- **TAR.GZ:** extract it and run `./camcraft-ui` from the extracted folder.
+- **AppImage:** `chmod +x` the file and run it; nothing is installed.
+- **Snap:** `sudo snap install --dangerous ./camcraft-*.snap`, then run
+  `camcraft`.
+- **Flatpak:** `flatpak install --user ./camcraft-*.flatpak`, then
+  `flatpak run io.github.NeoTech.Camcraft`. The Freedesktop runtime is
+  downloaded separately the first time.
+- **Arch Linux:** install the `pkg.tar.zst` from the release, or build the
+  recipe in the repository's `aur/` folder with `makepkg -si`.
+
+## macOS
+
+Open the DMG and drag `CamCraft.app` to Applications, or extract the ZIP.
+The app is ad-hoc signed and not notarized, so the first launch may need
+Control-click, then **Open**.
+
+## FreeBSD
+
+Extract the `freebsd-amd64.tar.gz` archive and run `camcraft-ui` from it.
+
+## What is in the archives
+
+The portable archives carry the desktop app (`camcraft-ui`), the
+command-line tool (`camcraft-cli`), the standalone post processor (`post`),
+and the assets the app needs: post processors, machine definitions, icons,
+fonts and themes.
+
+## Build from source
+
+You need Rust 1.90 or newer.
+
+```sh
+cargo run   --release -p camcraft-ui                       # build and start the app
+cargo build --release -p camcraft-app --bin camcraft-cli   # headless command line
+cargo build --release -p camcraft-post --bin post          # standalone post processor
+```

++++
+title = "Operations"
+description = "The operation kinds, their settings tabs, and generating toolpaths."
+weight = 4
++++
+
+An operation is one machining step: a tool, an area to cut, and how to cut
+it. The ribbon shows the operation groups the mounted machine can run, so a
+mill document has no turning operations and a lathe document no 3D
+milling. A mill-turn shows both.
+
+## Operation kinds
+
+| Group | Operations |
+|---|---|
+| Milling 2D | Face, Contour, Pocket, Slot, Trace, Adaptive, Offset, Engrave, Chamfer, Circular, Thread |
+| Milling 3D | 3D Pocket, 3D Finish, Deburr |
+| Drilling | Drill, Bore, Probe |
+| Multi-axis | 5-Axis Contour, 5-Axis Parallel, Swarf, Adv. Swarf, Rotary Contour, Rotary Parallel, Rotary Offset, Multi-Axis Rough, 5-Axis Flow, Multi-Axis Contour |
+| Turning | Facing, Profile Rough, Profile Finish, Groove Rough, Groove Finish, Part, Threading, Chamfer, Taper, Multi-Pass, Form, Bore |
+
+Some kinds carry several strategies. The 3D kinds cover adaptive roughing
+per level, waterline, parallel, scallop, radial, spiral, morph, flow,
+pencil and steep/shallow finishing. Drill covers spot, drill, peck, deep,
+tap and bore cycles, and **Detect holes** finds the holes in the model for
+you. Milling operations can also be indexed (3+2) to a tilted plane on a
+machine that can tilt.
+
+## The settings tabs
+
+An operation's page groups its settings on tabs. A kind shows only the
+tabs it has settings for:
+
+- **Geometry:** the tool and what to cut. Pick faces, edges or loops in
+  the viewport, then set containment, offset, extension and extra or open
+  boundaries where the kind has an area.
+- **Heights:** clearance, retract, top and bottom heights, and where each
+  is measured from.
+- **Passes:** stepover, stepdown, stock to leave and the kind's own
+  strategy settings.
+- **Lead in / Lead out:** how the tool enters, moves between levels and
+  leaves the cut, and the links between cuts.
+- **Feeds:** spindle speed and feed rates.
+- **Machine:** only on the few kinds that drive a machine function of
+  their own.
+
+Edits on a page are pending until you click **Apply** or **Generate**.
+Both are undoable with Ctrl+Z.
+
+## Generating
+
+**Generate** computes the toolpath and checks it. An operation can be in
+one of three states:
+
+- **No toolpath yet:** it has never been generated.
+- **Stale:** something it depends on (the model, the stock, the tool, the
+  work offset or its own settings) has changed since it was generated.
+  Generate it again.
+- **Generated:** the cached toolpath matches its inputs.
+
+When CamCraft cannot compute a safe path for some part of an operation, it
+does not hand you a partial or guessed one: generation stops with a
+message that names the setting or the geometry at fault. Moves the checks
+flag as unsafe are marked in the viewport, and a message that names a place
+can be clicked to frame it.
+
+## Checking
+
+- **Paths** shows every cached toolpath at once.
+- **Simulate** plays the program against the stock with a transport bar;
+  drag the playback slider to jump.
+- **Deviate** compares the machined stock with the model and colours where
+  material is left or where the program cut into the part. **Frame rest**
+  and **Frame gouge** take the view to the worst spot of each.

++++
+title = "Posting"
+description = "Writing the NC program, and what is checked first."
+weight = 5
++++
+
+Posting turns the document's operations into an NC program for one
+machine controller. Click **Post** (Ctrl+P), choose where to save the
+program, and CamCraft checks the program, writes it, and opens it in the
+G-code viewer.
+
+## Post processors
+
+The post is chosen on the **Post** page: a setup can pick its own, and a
+setup that picks none uses the document's. CamCraft ships posts for Fanuc,
+Haas, Siemens 840D, Heidenhain, Mazak, Tormach PathPilot, Makera Carvera and
+Fanuc Lathe. A post is a `.cps` script, so you can load your own with
+**Load post (.cps)**.
+
+The Post dialog opens where this document last posted, or beside the saved
+project with the project's name and the `.nc` extension.
+
+## What is checked before anything is written
+
+The post is a gate. It writes the program only when all of these hold:
+
+- every operation has a tool that exists and can cut that kind of
+  operation;
+- every operation has been generated, and nothing it depends on has
+  changed since (no **stale** operations);
+- no operation carries a warning;
+- the program as a whole verifies: the simulated stock shows no gouge into
+  the part, no move strikes a fixture, and no move exceeds a limit the
+  mounted machine states, such as axis travel or spindle speed.
+
+If any check fails, **nothing is written**; a program already at that path
+is left unchanged. See [Reading a refusal](@/guide/refusals.md).
+
+## More than one machine
+
+When setups use different machines or posts, Post writes one NC file per
+machine and post, and checks each one against its own machine.
+
+## Before you run it
+
+Passing the gate means CamCraft found nothing wrong with the program
+against the model, stock, fixtures and machine facts it knows. It does not
+know everything about your machine and setup. Read the program, run it in
+your control's own simulation if it has one, and dry-run it with the
+spindle off and Z raised before cutting material.
+
+## Headless posting
+
+The command-line tool `camcraft-cli` can drive CamCraft without the window,
+including as an MCP server for AI agents. The standalone `post` tool runs a
+`.cps` script over a cutter-location file; it does not run the document
+checks above, so its output is not verified.

++++
+title = "Reading a refusal"
+description = "Why CamCraft refused, and how to fix it."
+weight = 6
++++
+
+CamCraft refuses rather than guess. A refusal is not a crash: the document
+is unchanged and nothing unsafe was written. Every refusal names what is
+wrong, and usually what to do about it.
+
+## Where refusals appear
+
+- **A refused post** opens the **Post refused** window with the reason. It
+  says that nothing was written to the file, and that a program already
+  there is unchanged. The window stays until you close it, post
+  successfully, or open another document. If you edit the document while
+  it is open, it tells you the document has changed since, so post again
+  to check it.
+- **A refused change** (an edit, a new setup, a stock change) shows its
+  reason on the page you edited or on the status line, and the change is
+  not made.
+- **A refused generation** shows its reason on the operation's page. When
+  the reason names a place on the part, it is underlined: click it to
+  frame that spot in the viewport.
+- **A greyed-out button** says in its tooltip why it is unavailable.
+
+## Common post refusals
+
+| The message says | What it means | What to do |
+|---|---|---|
+| `<operation>: no toolpath yet - generate it first` | The operation was never generated. | Select it and click **Generate**. |
+| `<operation>: inputs moved since generation - regenerate before posting` | The model, stock, tool, work offset or the operation's settings changed after it was generated. | Generate it again. |
+| `post blocked - <operation>: <n> warning(s): ...` | The operation's own checks found something unsafe. | Read the warnings. The flagged moves are marked in the viewport; fix the setting or geometry they name. |
+| `gouge: program cuts below the model ...` | Simulating the whole program found material removed from the part. | Use **Simulate** and **Deviate** to find where, then fix the operation that cuts there. |
+| `... - fix the tool before posting` | An operation's tool is missing or cannot cut that kind of operation. | Pick a suitable tool on the operation's Geometry tab. |
+
+A machine-limit refusal names the axis or setting and the limit the
+mounted machine states. Either the program really is outside the machine's
+range (move the work offset or the part, or choose another machine), or
+the machine file's number is wrong (check it against the machine's
+manual).
+
+## When you think a refusal is wrong
+
+Report it on the
+[issue tracker](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues) with the
+message and, if you can, the project file. A refusal that blocks a safe
+program is a bug. A program that would gouge or collide and was **not**
+refused is a worse one: please report those first.

++++
+title = "Setups"
+description = "Stock, work offsets, machines, posts and fixtures, per setup."
+weight = 3
++++
+
+A setup is one way the part is held on one machine: its stock, its work
+offset, its machine and post, its fixtures and the tools it uses. A new
+document has no setups yet: its one stock and one work offset act as the
+first setup. Click **Create first setup** (Setup > Setups) to make it
+explicit, and **New setup** to add more, for example to flip the part and
+machine the other side.
+
+## The setup in the browser
+
+Each setup appears in the browser with its own pages:
+
+- **Settings:** whether it is the active setup, where its stock comes from,
+  how the part is aligned, and the WCS label the post writes.
+- **Machine:** the setup's machine. It can follow the document's machine
+  or carry its own. **Load machine (.mch)** loads a machine file.
+- **Post:** the post processor the setup writes with: a built-in post, or
+  **Load post (.cps)** for a script of your own.
+- **Fixtures:** vises, clamps and other workholding, imported or placed
+  from the fixture library.
+- **Tools:** the tools this setup's operations use, in change order.
+
+Below the pages, **Operations** lists the setup's operations.
+
+## Work offset
+
+Each setup owns one work coordinate system. G54 to G59 is only the label
+the post writes for it. Heights that are measured from the work offset read
+the setup's offset.
+
+## Carrying stock to the next setup
+
+**New setup** with **Carry stock and WCS over** ticked starts the new
+setup from a copy of the active setup's stock and work-offset placement;
+re-place the copy to describe how the part is re-clamped.
+
+On the Settings page of any setup after the first, the stock source can
+instead be what the setup before it leaves behind. Verification, rest
+machining and the fixture checks of that setup then see the material the
+earlier setup left, not the raw stock. CamCraft refuses that choice by
+name when it cannot verify the carry, for example between setups on
+different machines.
+
+## Machines
+
+The workspace button on the Setup group mounts a built-in machine for
+Milling, Turning or Mill-turning, and the ribbon shows only the operations
+that machine can run. CamCraft also ships machine files for several
+Tormach mills, and **View > Panels > Machines** browses, validates and
+edits `.mch` machine files.
+
+A machine file states facts such as axis travel, spindle speed range and
+rigid-tapping support. CamCraft checks a program against the facts the
+mounted machine states before it posts. A machine file is not a guarantee
+that a real machine is safe to run: check its numbers against your
+machine's manual.
+
+## Setups on different machines
+
+Setups can sit on different machines or posts. Each such group generates on
+its own machine, and Post writes one NC file per machine and post, each
+checked against its own machine.
+
+## Setup sheets
+
+The Setups page lists each setup's tools in change order, with cut and
+rapid lengths and the estimated time. **Export setup sheets…** writes one
+text page per setup. Posting does not write them.
